title: CoralTemp SST steps in 1995, 2002 and 2008, confirmed by ESA CCI and moorings, make the CRW bleaching baseline 0.06-0.14 C too cold; 2023-25 Alert Level 2 falls from 91% to 72-81% of 214 reef stations
abstract: Question: NOAA Coral Reef Watch (CRW) calculates bleaching heat stress (HotSpot, Degree Heating Week DHW) from CoralTemp v3.1, with a baseline (MMM) fixed from 1985-2012. Two earlier campaign studies found CoralTemp steps but disagreed on their effect on recent bleaching events. Is CoralTemp homogeneous against a fully independent satellite record, and what do its steps do to the official CRW station heat stress? Approach: we compared CoralTemp monthly SST at about 30,000 one-degree sample pixels (60S-60N, 1985-2026) with ESA SST CCI v3.0.1 on the same pixels, HadSST4.2, ERSSTv5, COBE-SST2, DOISST and OI v2, with exact segmentation, control pairs, daily dating, 10-degree maps and 148 moored buoys. We recalculated DHW at all 214 CRW Regional Virtual Stations after a local step correction, for five step sets and several references. Results: CoralTemp has steps of -0.06 to -0.11 C in June 1995, +0.08 to +0.11 C in July 2002 (18-24 July in CCI daily data, four months before the documented November 2002 splice) and +0.05 to +0.08 C on 1 January 2008. CCI confirms them (z -5.2, +7.0, +12.9; 98% of 10-degree boxes positive in 2002 and 2008). Tropical moorings confirm them (98-100% of 59-88 GTMBA moorings). They cause all of the 0.022-0.036 C per decade faster warming of CoralTemp. Because they lie inside the baseline window, the CRW MMM is too cold by a median 0.08 C (0.06-0.14 C). The share of stations at Alert Level 2 (DHW >= 8) in 2023-2025 falls from 91% to 78% (72-81% over all variants; 30 of 214 stations lose it). The 2014-2017 share falls from 68% to 42-57%, the 1998 share rises from 21% to 26-35%, and the DHW trend falls by 23% (19-31%). Any warm step inside 1985-2012 gives the modern decrease; at DHW >= 4 the 2023-2025 change is small (2-8 points) because that level is saturated, which explains the earlier disagreement. Limitations: the references have own errors of about 0.03 C; the correction is regional, not reef-pixel based; coastal subtropical buoys do not show the 2008 step; the causes of the steps are not proven.
